title: The pluperfect: what had happened before the crash

sections.content: You know the *pluscuamperfecto* (*había* + past participle) from B1 Unit 1: it describes something that had already happened before another moment in the past. It helps you explain what had been going on before 1929 and what the crisis found when it arrived. *Ya* (already) often goes with it.

items.spanish: Cuando llegó la crisis, muchos países ya habían pedido grandes préstamos.
items.english: When the crisis came, many countries had already asked for large loans.

items.spanish: Antes de 1929, los precios de las acciones habían subido mucho.
items.english: Before 1929 the prices of shares had risen a lot.

items.spanish: Muchas personas habían comprado acciones con dinero prestado.
items.english: Many people had bought shares with borrowed money.

items.spanish: Los bancos ya habían prestado mucho dinero a varios gobiernos.
items.english: The banks had already lent a lot of money to several governments.

sections.content: Use the *pluscuamperfecto* for the earlier event and the preterite for the later one: *cuando llegó la crisis* (later) *ya habían pedido préstamos* (earlier). Nothing goes between *habían* and the participle: *ya habían pedido*, not *habían ya pedido*.
